Straightening your teeth doesn’t have to mean rearranging your life.

What Are Clear Aligners?

Clear aligners are a series of custom, transparent plastic trays that gradually shift teeth into a straighter position. Each set is worn for a set number of days before you move on to the next in the sequence, with small adjustments built into every tray. Because they’re removable, you can eat, brush, and floss without the brackets and wires that come with traditional braces.

How Clear Aligners in Wauwatosa Work

Treatment starts with a consultation where we review your bite, take digital images, and map out a plan. We use the Candid Pro clear aligner system to design trays that apply steady, gentle pressure over time. Most patients wear their aligners for 20 to 22 hours a day, removing them only to eat or clean their teeth. Depending on how much movement is needed, treatment can last anywhere from a few months to over a year, and we schedule regular check-ins to track progress and ensure the plan remains on target.

A few things shape how your treatment unfolds:

  • The starting position of your teeth and bite
  • How consistently you wear your trays each day
  • Whether any refinements are needed partway through treatment

Fitting Aligners Into Daily Life

Once you get into a rhythm, wearing aligners becomes second nature. You’ll want to keep a small case on hand, so you have somewhere to put your trays while you eat, and a quick rinse before popping them back in goes a long way. Many patients find hygiene is actually simpler than with wires and brackets, since there’s nothing to floss around.

  • Set a phone reminder to help track wear time.
  • Pack a travel kit with a toothbrush and case.
  • Rinse trays after meals before reinserting them.

Beyond Alignment: Cosmetic and Family Care

Straightening your teeth is often just one part of a larger goal. For patients interested in refining the shape or color of their teeth once alignment is complete, Dr. Laura Russell performs no-prep veneer treatments as a conservative option. If your case involves more extensive rebuilding, our full mouth reconstruction services can address structural and cosmetic needs together. For families juggling multiple appointments, our team includes dentists who focus on different stages of care, so kids and adults can often be seen under the same roof. We also offer a broader range of dental services, including restorative dentistry for patients who need repair work as part of their alignment plan. If you’re interested in the specifics of the aligner system itself, you can read more about our clear aligner treatment options.

Caring for Your Aligners

Good habits during treatment protect both your trays and your teeth. Clean your aligners with the solution we recommend rather than hot water, which can warp the plastic, and store them in their case anytime they’re out of your mouth. Sticking to your regular dental visits during treatment also gives us a chance to catch issues early and keep your oral hygiene on track.

  • Rinse trays daily and brush gently with a soft brush.
  • Store trays properly when eating or drinking.
  • Keep up with scheduled visits throughout treatment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do clear aligners work for adults and teens?

Yes. Aligners can address a wide range of alignment issues for both age groups, though we evaluate each case individually to confirm they’re the right fit.

Will I need to change my diet?

Not really. Since trays come out to eat, you can keep your usual habits, just remember to brush before putting your aligners back in.

Most patients move into a retainer phase to hold their new alignment in place, which we’ll go over in detail as you near the end of your treatment plan.

No temporary crown, no second appointment, no waiting weeks for a lab to send something back. We handle the entire process on-site, from scanning the tooth to milling and bonding the crown, so you can get back to your day without delays.

What Are Same-Day Crowns?

A traditional crown requires two visits: one to prepare the tooth and place a temporary crown, and another to cement the permanent crown after the lab finishes it. Same-day crowns cut that process down to a single appointment. We use a digital scanner to capture the shape of the prepared tooth, then a milling machine fabricates a ceramic crown right here in our office while you wait. Once it’s ready, we check the fit, adjust the bite, and bond it permanently before you leave.

Ceramic crowns resist staining and blend with surrounding teeth, so the result looks natural. Skipping the temporary also reduces the chances of the tooth shifting or becoming sensitive between visits.

Who Makes a Good Candidate?

Most adults dealing with a cracked tooth, a large or failing filling, or significant decay are strong candidates for a crown. To qualify for same-day treatment specifically, the tooth needs enough remaining structure to support a restoration, and the surrounding gum tissue should be healthy.

During your appointment, we take X-rays and digital scans to assess:

  • The extent of damage or decay
  • Gum health and bone support around the tooth
  • How the crown will interact with your bite and opposing teeth

If the tooth is too compromised or there’s an active infection, we’ll talk through other options, including bridges or implants, as part of a longer-term plan for that area of your mouth.

Same-Day Crowns in Wauwatosa: What to Expect at Your Visit

The appointment starts with a review of your X-rays and a conversation about what’s happening with the tooth. Local anesthetic keeps you comfortable during preparation, and a digital scan replaces the traditional tray impression, which most patients find much easier to tolerate. While the crown mills on-site, you’re free to relax in our reception area.

Once the crown is ready, we check the color, fit, and bite before bonding it in place. Minor adjustments are made right then, and we walk you through the care instructions before you head out. The whole appointment typically runs a few hours, but you leave with a permanent crown, not a placeholder.

Our dental team includes Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego. Dr. Hoyme handles most pediatric care, while Dr. Russell focuses on esthetic restorations. For questions about which provider makes sense for your situation, our contact page makes it easy to reach us.

Caring for Your Crown After Placement

Same-day crowns are durable, but the first 24 hours matter while the bonding fully sets. A few things to keep in mind:

  • Stick to soft foods and avoid anything sticky or hard for the rest of the day.
  • Brush twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush and floss gently at the gumline.
  • Some mild sensitivity in the first few days is normal; call us if pain increases or lingers.
  • If you grind your teeth at night, a night guard protects the crown from excess wear.

Routine checkups let us keep an eye on how the crown is holding up and catch any issues early, before they become bigger problems.

Why December Matters for Your Dental Coverage

Here’s something most people don’t think about until it’s too late. Your dental insurance operates on an annual maximum, usually between $1,000 and $2,000, depending on your plan. Once January 1st rolls around, that unused portion doesn’t roll over. It just disappears. Gone. Like it never existed.

Think about it this way. If you’ve only used $500 of a $1,500 annual maximum, you’re leaving $1,000 behind. That’s real money that could go toward treatments you actually need. Plus, many plans have already covered your deductible by this point in the year, so your out-of-pocket costs are even lower right now than in January when everything resets.

Cosmetic enhancements. Dr. Laura Russell specializes in no-prep veneer treatments that transform smiles without extensive tooth preparation. The Two-Visit Classic: Traditional Crowns Take Their Time

Traditional crowns follow a time-tested process. During the first appointment, the dentist reshapes the tooth, takes an impression, and places a temporary crown. You wait about two weeks while the dental lab makes the final crown.

Once the crown comes back, you return for a second appointment. The dentist checks the fit and cements it into place. This method works, but it requires more time and a little more patience.

Fast Track Fame: Same-Day Crowns Steal the Scene

Same-day crowns change the game completely. Our office uses CAD/CAM technology to scan your tooth, design your crown digitally, and mill it in-house while you relax in the chair.

The dentist cements your crown the same day. There’s no need for a second visit, no temporary crown, or putty impressions. It’s fast, efficient, and ideal for patients who want results now.

Side-by-Side Style: Let’s Compare Crowns

When you weigh your crown options, each offers something different. The best choice depends on your priorities, schedule, and dental needs.

Same-Day Crowns

  • Made and placed in a single appointment
  • Designed with digital imaging
  • No need for temporary crowns
  • Durable, tooth-colored ceramic
  • Perfect for busy patients

Traditional Crowns

  • Usually completed in two visits
  • Often uses physical molds
  • Requires temporary crowns
  • May offer more material choices
  • Better in rare cases with complex shaping needs

Fit, Form, and Function: Who Wears It Best?

Same-day crowns fit just as well as traditional ones. Our technology produces highly accurate digital impressions, and the crown gets milled with extreme precision. The dentist can make quick adjustments on the spot.

Both types restore function, protect the tooth, and improve your smile. However, same-day crowns offer an edge in comfort and efficiency. Most patients appreciate getting everything done without the extra visit or added inconvenience.

Who Needs a Crown Anyway?

Crowns don’t just improve your smile. They repair, protect, and restore damaged teeth. The dentist may recommend a crown when the tooth’s structure becomes too weak for a filling or veneer.

Common reasons for a crown include:

  • A cracked or fractured tooth
  • A root canal-treated tooth
  • Severe tooth decay
  • Worn-down or misshapen teeth
  • Old crowns that need replacing

No More Temporaries, No More Guessing

Temporary crowns tend to fall off at the worst time. They don’t always fit perfectly and rarely look as good as the final version. Same-day crowns eliminate the need for this short-term fix.

You leave the office with your final crown already in place. There’s no delay, no risk of breakage, and no awkward in-between period.

  • Periodontal Therapy: Treat gum disease before placing crowns to ensure a healthy foundation that supports your new restorations.

You don’t need special tools or expensive products to care for a crown. Brush and floss normally, and avoid chewing hard items like ice or pens. Our team will check your crown during cleanings to ensure everything stays on track.

What Makes Dental Implants in Wauwatosa So Awesome?

Dental implants do more than fill gaps. They protect your jawbone, support your facial structure, and restore your ability to chew everything from steak to salad. Unlike dentures, implants don’t slip or click. The dentist places a titanium post into your jawbone; over time, it bonds with the bone to become a strong foundation for your new tooth.

Why Our Patients Love Dental Implants

Our patients in Wauwatosa choose implants for lots of good reasons:

  • They look natural

  • They stay in place

  • They prevent bone loss

  • They boost self-esteem

Dr. Hoyme and the rest of our team want you to feel informed and confident at every stage of your dental implant journey. We use advanced technology to make the process more precise, comfortable, and successful, from start to finish.

  1. Consultation and Planning

    The doctor begins by evaluating your oral and overall health. We use advanced 3D cone beam imaging to get a detailed view of your jawbone and surrounding structures. This technology helps us measure bone density, map nerves, and design a surgical guide that ensures pinpoint accuracy. The dentist then creates a customized treatment plan, tailored to your smile goals and anatomy.

  2. Placement


    Using digital planning tools and guided implant technology, the doctor places the titanium post into your jawbone with exceptional precision. Because of this technology, the procedure usually takes less time and causes less discomfort. The dentist may use a surgical guide to position the implant exactly where it needs to go, minimizing guesswork and maximizing long-term success.

  3. Healing Time

    Over the next few months, your jawbone naturally fuses with the implant post. This process, called osseointegration, builds a stable foundation for your new tooth. During this time, we check in with you to monitor healing using digital scans, not just a visual check. Most patients say the recovery feels easier than expected, thanks in part to the precision of the placement.

  4. Restoration

    Once healing is complete, we attach a custom crown that looks and feels like a natural tooth. We design the crown with digital impressions, which means no gooey trays and no guesswork. The result is a seamless match that fits your bite, smile, and personality.

  5. Maintenance and Smile Finishing Touches

At each visit, the dentist checks the implant’s integrity and ensures your gum tissue stays strong. The Importance of Oral Health and Understanding Periodontal Disease

Oral health is a critical component of overall well-being. Maintaining healthy teeth and gums involves regular brushing, flossing, and routine dental check-ups. These practices help prevent the onset of periodontal disease, a common condition affecting many adults. Periodontal or gum disease occurs when the gums become inflamed and infected due to plaque buildup. If left untreated, it can lead to tooth loss and other serious health issues.

Periodontal disease ranges from simple gum inflammation, known as gingivitis, to more severe infections, called periodontitis. Symptoms include red, swollen gums that bleed easily, persistent bad breath, and loose teeth. The progression of gum disease can be halted with proper dental care, emphasizing the importance of early detection and treatment.

Laser Treatment for Periodontal Disease: A Modern Solution

Laser treatment for periodontal disease represents a modern solution to a traditional problem. This method uses precise laser beams to target and remove the infected gum tissue without harming the surrounding healthy tissue. It’s a less invasive alternative to conventional surgery, offering reduced discomfort and quicker patient recovery time.

Advantages of Laser Treatment for Gum Disease

The benefits of laser treatment for gum disease are numerous. Patients experience less swelling, bleeding, and discomfort than traditional surgery. The precision of the laser allows for targeted therapy, preserving more of the healthy tissue. Why Dental 3D Printing Matters 

Dental 3D printing has revolutionized how dental procedures are approached, from the planning stages to execution. Digital technology allows for the precise creation of dental models, prosthetics, and even orthodontic devices. The accuracy it offers minimizes room for error, and every dental appliance is custom-fit to the patient. For those invested in their health, this means a smoother, quicker, and more comfortable experience when undergoing dental procedures.

How 3D Printing Works

Dental 3D printing operates through an additive manufacturing process, where dental devices and structures are constructed layer by layer from a digital model. First, a detailed digital scan of the patient’s mouth or the required dental structure is obtained. The digital impression is then transferred to specialized software, where it can be manipulated and refined as necessary. 

Once the digital design is complete, the 3D printer uses dental-specific materials—like resins or ceramic composites—to methodically lay down successive thin layers until the entire structure forms. This layer-by-layer creation allows for intricate designs, accurate fittings, and customized solutions that fit each patient’s unique dental anatomy.

Advantages of This Process

The integration of 3D printing in dentistry presents a multitude of benefits:

  1. Speed and Efficiency: Traditional methods of creating dental molds or devices can be time-consuming. 3D printing accelerates this process, meaning patients can receive their custom dental solutions faster than ever before.
  2. Enhanced Precision: 3D printing operates with digital precision. This guarantees that digital impressions, whether it’s a crown, bridge, or retainer, fit perfectly to the individual’s unique dental structure.
  3. Cost-effective: As technology advances, it’s becoming a more affordable option, which translates to cost savings for both the dental practice and, ultimately, the patient.
  4. Innovative Solutions: From dental implants to full dentures, 3D printing creates a broader range of dental solutions that weren’t feasible with older techniques.

How Long 3D Printed Teeth Last

The longevity of 3D-printed teeth largely depends on the material used, the type of dental appliance, and the care taken by the patient. Generally, 3D-printed dental restorations, such as crowns or bridges made from high-quality resins or ceramic composites, can last anywhere from several years to over a decade, rivaling the durability of traditionally crafted restorations.

Understanding the Dental Implant Procedure

According to the National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, adults 20 to 64 years old have 25 of their 32 natural teeth remaining on average. Dental implants are a beneficial tooth replacement option for many of these adults. Traditional implants restore lost teeth by replacing them with artificial ones that mimic natural teeth in appearance and function. 

The procedure typically involves placing a titanium post into the jawbone, serving as a sturdy base for the new tooth. Once integrated and healed, a crown resembling your natural tooth will be placed atop the implant. This comprehensive approach achieves both functionality and aesthetic appeal.

Types of Dental Implant Positioning

Dental implant services have revolutionized restorative dentistry, allowing patients to regain their natural smile permanently. Among the various implant techniques, two are particularly prevalent. Both techniques cater to specific patient needs for optimal results and comfort.

  • Endosteal implants: These implants are the most common, involving titanium screws placed directly into the jawbone, serving as artificial tooth roots. Once healed, these screws anchor the replacement teeth. 
  • Subperiosteal implants: This option is designed for those with a shallow jawbone who cannot or do not wish to undergo a procedure to rebuild it. These implants sit atop the jawbone but beneath the gum line.

Types of Dental Implant Materials

Tooth replacement implants are crafted with materials specifically chosen for their strength and aesthetic qualities for seamless integration into place. 

  • Titanium implants: Titanium has been the go-to material for dental implants for decades. This material is commonly used for its exceptional ability to fuse with the jawbone in a process known as osseointegration. Its inherent strength and biocompatibility make it a preferred choice for endosteal implants. 
  • Zirconia implants: Often called ceramic implants, zirconia stands out for its metal-free composition. This material offers a white color that many find aesthetically appealing, especially for patients with thin or receding gums where metal implants might appear. Both materials are renowned for their durability and compatibility, providing patients with long-lasting and safe implant solutions.

Benefits of Opting for Dental Implants

Dental implants have several advantages over conventional solutions like dentures or bridges. Firstly, they provide a permanent solution, reducing the hassle of maintenance or replacements. 

Secondly, they integrate with your jawbone. With unmatched stability, you can eat, speak, and laugh with the same confidence as natural teeth. Dental implants help maintain your facial structure and jawbone, preventing the sunken appearance that can occur with missing teeth.

Maintaining Clean Oral Health at Home

Maintaining a clean, healthy mouth at home is essential for great oral health. Start with the basics: brush your teeth at least twice daily using fluoride toothpaste, and don’t rush – spend about two minutes each time. Make sure to reach all areas, including the back teeth and along the gum line. Daily flossing helps remove food particles and plaque from areas your toothbrush can’t reach. Consider using mouthwash, as it can help reduce the risk of decay, gum disease, and bad breath.

Additionally, be mindful of your diet. Consider limiting sugary snacks and drinks. Try to consume a diet rich in vitamins, minerals, and fresh fruits and vegetables. Regularly drinking water also helps wash away food particles and hydrate your mouth. Lastly, remember to replace your toothbrush every 3 to 4 months. Replace them sooner if the bristles have become frayed. When performed consistently, this simple routine can help keep your teeth clean and your smile radiant between dentist appointments.

Why Routine Appointments Shouldn’t Be Skipped

Delaying or dismissing a dental visit can be easy, particularly if you aren’t experiencing any overt dental issues. However, such a decision could have serious implications for your oral health. Many dental problems, such as cavities or gum disease, may manifest noticeable symptoms once they are advanced and require significant intervention. At MidTown Dental in Milwaukee, we’ve dedicated over 25 years to empowering families with the right information and quality care to maintain healthy smiles for their children. Here are 5 essential tips that every parent should know regarding their child’s oral health.

1. Routine Dental Appointments are Essential

Pediatric dental care goes beyond regular tooth brushing. It’s a specialized form of dentistry that involves diagnosing, preventing, and treating oral health issues in children from infancy through adolescence. The key is to instill good dental habits from an early age and ensure regular check-ups, which are paramount to the early detection and prevention of potential oral health issues.

2. Oral Care Should Begin Even Before Your Child Has Teeth

This might seem surprising, but the rationale is rooted in preventative care. A baby’s mouth can still host harmful bacteria, which can affect emerging teeth and cause future dental problems. By gently cleaning a baby’s gums with a soft, damp cloth after feedings, parents can help keep these bacteria at bay, paving the way for a healthier oral environment when those first teeth arrive. 

Establishing this routine early on also sets the stage for future good dental hygiene habits, emphasizing the importance of oral care from a very young age. Proactive oral care from infancy forms the cornerstone for healthy gums and teeth throughout their lifetime.

3. The Importance of Establishing a Routine

You can begin by cleaning your baby’s gums with a soft, damp cloth before their first tooth appears. Once teeth emerge, use a soft-bristled toothbrush with fluoride toothpaste. As your child ages, teach them to brush twice daily and introduce flossing. You can also limit sugary snacks and drinks to maintain your child’s oral health. Regularly scheduled dental check-ups can also help detect any early signs of cavities and allow for timely interventions.

4. The Role of Fluoride and Sealants in Pediatric Dental Care

Fluoride is a vital mineral that helps harden tooth enamel and prevents decay. It’s often found in tap water, certain foods, and many kinds of toothpaste. However, your child might need additional fluoride treatment if they’re at high risk for cavities.

Another effective way to protect your child’s teeth is with dental sealants. These thin, protective coatings applied to the back teeth can prevent food and plaque from getting stuck in the grooves, reducing the risk of cavities by up to 80%.

5. Dentist Visits Can Be Fun

Children, like adults, may experience dental anxiety. Create a positive impression about dental visits through stories and role-play. Regular dental visits from a young age can also help your child familiarize themselves with the dental office environment, making appointments less stressful. Our team at MidTown Dental takes pride in creating a comforting atmosphere for our young patients.

Why a Dentist Teeth Cleaning is Important

Usually, the body’s natural defenses and good oral health care, such as daily brushing and flossing, keep bacteria under control. However, without some additional oral hygiene steps, bacteria can reach levels that might lead to oral infections.

Professional teeth cleanings can give you a sparkling, confident smile and play a key role in combating gum diseases and tooth decay. This bi-annual procedure involves the removal of plaque and tartar build-up, which are responsible for cavities, gum infections, and bad breath. Regular cleanings are preventative, catching minor issues before they escalate into severe problems that demand complex treatments. 

Proactive Measures for Sustainable Oral Health

Now that you understand the importance of professional cleanings, let’s dive into the daily habits that can extend the benefits of your dental appointments:

  1. Regular Brushing and Flossing: Brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and flossing at least once daily is foundational. It helps remove food particles stuck between your teeth and prevents plaque build-up.
  2. Healthy Diet: Avoid excessively consuming sugary and acidic foods and beverages. These erode the enamel, causing cavities and sensitivity. Instead, opt for a balanced diet rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber.
  3. Stay Hydrated: Drinking plenty of water ensures a clean mouth by washing away food debris and promoting saliva production, which naturally fights bacteria.

What to Avoid After a Dental Cleaning

After a thorough cleaning at your dentist’s office, there are a few things to avoid to preserve the pristine condition of your teeth:

  • Avoid eating foods with strong colors for a few hours as your teeth might be more susceptible to staining after a cleaning.
  • Waiting an hour after your appointment before eating or drinking is advisable.
  • If you have had fluoride treatment, refrain from oral care routines for at least 30 minutes post-procedure.

What Happens During a Routine Checkup

While these personal dental care tips are important, they don’t replace regular dental checkups. Regular dental checkups are the key to optimum oral health. Professional examinations help detect potential issues that often go unnoticed in routine home care. 

A typical dental cleaning starts with a physical examination of your oral cavity. Your hygienist uses a small mirror to check around your teeth and gums for any signs of concern, such as gingivitis or other potential issues. 

Next is removing plaque and tartar build-up around the gum line and between your teeth using a scaler. Depending on the amount of tartar, this could take some time. The cleaning process is followed by a high-powered electric brush and professional toothpaste for a thorough brushing. This helps remove any excess tartar and gives your teeth a deep clean. 

Following this, your hygienist will floss your teeth to remove anything left behind after the brushing. After flossing, you rinse to get rid of debris. The cleaning procedure typically ends with a fluoride treatment, which serves as a ‘protective barrier’ for your teeth to help fight against cavities for several months.

What is Clear Aligner Therapy?

Clear aligner therapy is a modern orthodontic treatment that uses multiple clear, removable aligners to straighten teeth gradually. Unlike traditional braces that use wires and brackets, clear aligner therapy aligners are made from a transparent plastic material that is virtually invisible when worn. This innovative process allows patients to straighten their teeth without feeling self-conscious about their appearance.

How Does Clear Aligner Therapy Work?

First, we take digital impressions of your teeth to create a 3D mouth model. Our dental technicians use this model to create a customized treatment plan that involves a series of clear aligners. Each set of aligners shifts your teeth into the desired position gradually. You will wear each aligner for a specified period, typically two weeks, before moving on to the next aligner in the series. The number of aligners you will need will depend on your specific case.

Who Can Benefit from Clear Aligner Therapy?

Clear aligners are an excellent option for anyone seeking to straighten their teeth, from teenagers to adults. It is especially ideal for busy professionals who may not have the time or desire to wear traditional braces. These aligners can correct many orthodontic issues, including crooked teeth, crowded teeth, overbites, underbites, and crossbites.

What to Expect When You Choose Clear Aligner Therapy at MidTown Dental Care

Personalized Treatment Plan

  • Our dental technicians use SureSmile and Invisalign products to create clear aligners that will gradually shift your teeth.

Comfortable Treatment

  • Clear aligners are a comfortable and low-profile orthodontic treatment. The aligners are gentle on your teeth and gums because they are made from smooth, flexible plastic.
  • The aligners are removable, so you can remove them to eat, brush, and floss. This makes it easy to maintain good oral hygiene during your treatment.

title: How An Implant Overdenture Can Improve Your Quality Of Life
heading: How Implant Overdenture Can Improve Your Quality of Life
description: Modern dental technology has come a long way, & an implant overdenture option has become a highly effective solution if you've lost teeth!
excerpt: If you have lost most or all of your teeth, then you know how hard it can be to eat your favorite foods, smile confidently, and speak clearly. Thankfully, modern dental technology has…
html:
If you have lost most or all of your teeth, then you know how hard it can be to eat your favorite foods, smile confidently, and speak clearly. Thankfully, modern dental technology has come a long way, and the implant overdenture option has become a highly effective solution for many. In this blog, we’ll explore implant overdentures, how they can improve your quality of life, and how to care for them after receiving care at MidTown Dental Care in Milwaukee.

What are Implant Overdentures?

Implant overdentures are a type of dental prosthesis that attaches to dental implants. Unlike traditional dentures that come into direct contact with the gums, an implant overdenture device is anchored in place by surgically impacted posts in the jawbone. The result is a secure and stable dental appliance that looks and feels like natural teeth.

The implants are made of titanium, a strong and durable metal well-tolerated by the human body. The overdenture, on the other hand, can be made from a variety of materials, including:

Acrylic

Acrylic is a common type of plastic in dentures. It is lightweight, durable, and easy to adjust. Acrylic dentures are also relatively inexpensive.

Porcelain

Porcelain is a ceramic used often in crowns and veneers. It is solid and durable and has a natural appearance that closely resembles tooth enamel.

Zirconia

Zirconia is a type of ceramic that is becoming increasingly popular in dentistry. It is highly durable and has a natural appearance that looks almost identical to tooth enamel. Zirconia is also biocompatible, which means it adapts to the human body.

Implant overdentures are designed to ensure that patients can enjoy the confidence of a complete set of teeth. These prostheses are composed of three main parts, including surgically implanted posts, connecting components such as abutments and clip attachments, and the denture itself. The posts are made of durable materials that can integrate seamlessly with the jawbone, providing a stable foundation for the denture. The connecting components, including abutments and clip attachments, allow the denture to be securely attached to the posts, ensuring that it stays in place while also being easy to remove for cleaning. Individual adjustments to an implant overdenture device can be made to the hardware for a personalized fit, ensuring maximum comfort and functionality. 

Benefits of an Implant Overdenture Device

Implant overdenture benefits are numerous over traditional dentures. First, they provide a more natural and comfortable fit. Traditional dentures can often slip or move around in the mouth, leading to discomfort and embarrassment. On the other hand, implant overdentures are firmly anchored in place, making them much more stable and comfortable.

Implant overdentures also improve your oral health. When you lose teeth, the underlying bone in your jaw can deteriorate. Implant overdentures help to prevent this by stimulating the bone and promoting new growth. This intervention can help preserve your jaw’s structure and prevent further tooth loss.

Finally, implant overdentures provide a much more natural-looking smile. Unlike traditional dentures, which can often look fake or unnatural, implant overdentures are custom-made to match the shape and color of your existing teeth. This realistic look makes them virtually indistinguishable from natural teeth, giving you the confidence to smile, speak, and be you!

Caring for Implant Overdentures

Caring for implant overdentures is relatively easy. You will brush and floss your teeth regularly, just as you would with natural teeth. You should still visit your dentist regularly for check-ups and teeth cleanings. Additionally, you may need to use a special type of toothbrush or dental floss designed for dental implants. It’s also essential to avoid certain foods and habits that can damage your implant overdentures. For example, you should avoid chewing on hard objects like ice or popcorn kernels, which can damage the implant posts. It would be best to avoid smoking, which can increase your risk of implant failure.

Smile Confidently With Your Implant Overdenture

If you are missing teeth, the implant overdenture option may be an excellent solution. It offers several benefits over traditional dentures, including a more natural and comfortable fit, improved oral health, and a more natural-looking smile. To learn more about implant overdentures or would like to request a quote, contact MidTown Dental Care today. Our experienced team of dental professionals looks forward to helping you achieve a confident smile.

title: Important Things To Know About Dental Care For Kids
heading: 6 Important Things to Know About Dental Care For Kids
description: To help ensure your child's dental health, it's important to know what to prioritize when it comes to dental care for kids. Click for more!
excerpt: Dental care should be a top priority for your child’s overall health. Indeed, caring for teeth and gums from an early age can do wonders to prevent cavities, gum disease, and other…
html:
Dental care should be a top priority for your child’s overall health. Indeed, caring for teeth and gums from an early age can do wonders to prevent cavities, gum disease, and other various dental problems down the road. Along with steps you will want to take at home, you will also want to establish regular visits with your dentist at MidTown Dental Care in Milwaukee. In addition to that, when deciding what to prioritize when it comes to dental care for kids, keep at least these few tips in mind. 

They Should Start Coming To Dental Appointments At A Young Age

The American Dental Association (ADA) recommends that children first visit their dentist when their first baby teeth emerge or at least once before the age of one. Basically, you will want to book an appointment at the time at which either of these events occurs first. Establishing a dentist at this young age and continuing to attend regular appointments will allow for the diagnosis and treatment of any issues as soon as they arise. 

In addition to setting a child’s first dental appointment in a timely manner, you will also want to establish regular visits to the dentist for checkups and cleanings. These continued consultations will help us keep an eye on your child’s oral health as well as make timely recommendations as they grow. 

They Need To Be Acclimated To The Dentist’s Office

Many children may be uncomfortable or even frightened when they first attend a dental appointment, just as they may be at other medical assessments. However, there are a variety of ways to help a child establish a positive perspective on the dentist’s office, and it all starts with their first visit. At MidTown Dental Care, we work hard to make your child as comfortable as possible at our office when they attend their pediatric dental appointments. We teach them about the different dental gadgets and help them understand the importance of ongoing dental care. 

They Should Brush Everyday

As soon as your child’s first tooth emerges, you will want to start brushing or cleaning every day. As children age, you will want to teach them about brushing habits. Flossing will also become important when your child’s teeth start to touch one another. At that point, they should be brushing and flossing every day as the start of a highly beneficial lifelong process. These daily activities will help prevent food buildup and the development of cavities or the breakdown of tooth enamel. Be sure to ask your dentist for more habits to establish with your child for good dental health. 

Choose The Right Toothbrush

Before you start to brush their teeth, it will be important to choose the right toothbrush for your child. The brush should be the correct size and shape for your child’s mouth, and generally will be one made specifically for children. These toothbrushes will generally be better suited to children as well as more fun for them to use. They may have more fun designs and colors along with a wider grip for their hands. Be sure also to replace your child’s toothbrush at least every three months or when the bristles start to fray or break down. 

Limit Sugary Drinks & Snacks

As your child continues to grow, it will be important to keep sugary treats to a minimum in order to avoid tooth decay and cavities. Regularly consuming a lot of sugary foods and drinks can have a variety of other health benefits for growing children, so it is a good practice to establish from a young age. You can limit the number of sugary foods and beverages you keep in the house as well as make sure your child is drinking water regularly throughout the day, which can help curb sugar cravings. 

See Your Dentist For The Best Dental Care For Kids

No matter if it’s the first appointment for your kid, their annual exam, or the first one after a gap, it is probably time to bring them in for an appointment! Let the dental professionals at MidTown Dental Care answer your questions about teaching your child to properly brush and floss and what toothbrush to choose. And let us help your child come to see oral health as an empowering daily activity. We know that dental care for kids doesn’t have to be boring or tedious! Request a pediatric dentistry appointment with us today.

title: 10 Steps for Deep Cleaning Teeth | MidTown Dental Care
heading: 10 Steps for Deep Cleaning Teeth
description: While brushing & flossing is great to do, there are more steps to take when it comes to deep cleaning teeth. Click for more information!
excerpt: Regularly brushing and flossing your teeth is tremendously beneficial. Not only will the process help to keep your gums and teeth looking great but it will also keep them healthy and…
html:
Regularly brushing and flossing your teeth is tremendously beneficial. Not only will the process help to keep your gums and teeth looking great but it will also keep them healthy and strong. Of course, the dental hygienists at MidTown Dental Care in Milwaukee are here to support your teeth health at your regular visits, but we also want to make sure you are well informed on the steps to take every day to keep your teeth healthy and strong. Keep reading for our Essential tips on deep cleaning teeth and gums.

1. Regularly Brush Your Teeth

Let’s start with the most obvious, but also the most important, for maintaining proper oral hygiene. Brush your teeth every day, at least twice a day. For best results, be sure you’re brushing for two minutes and with high-quality fluoride toothpaste. 

2. Use A Soft Toothbrush

When brushing your teeth daily, use a soft bristle toothbrush. Soft bristles will help you avoid aggravating your gums, which can lead to receding gums. Soft toothbrushes and gentle brushing habits will also help in maintaining your enamel. The electric toothbrush is a good investment as it has a soft brush head but also allows you to have a controlled brushing technique while keeping track of how long you have been brushing your teeth. 

3. Floss Daily 

After brushing your teeth, floss. thoroughly floss between teeth in order to remove any food particles that brushing might miss. Flossing is an excellent way to prevent plaque buildup and helps maintain healthy gums.  

4. Remove Debris & Plaque

While floss is a great way to remove food particles and plaque, some debris and plaque buildup may still persist. For additional cleaning power, use things like dental picks, interdental brushes, and tongue scrapers. Talk with your dentist about what tools might work best for you.  

5. Use Mouthwash

Rinsing with an antibacterial mouthwash can help keep your teeth clean and sparkling. It also can freshen your breath and prevent plaque accumulation that can lead to bigger issues over time. 

6. Schedule Regular Cleanings

We can’t stress this one enough: Schedule and keep dental checkups and dental cleanings throughout the year. The rule of thumb is a checkup once a year and cleanings every six months. Professional dental cleanings are an essential part of maintaining a healthy mouth as the tools and materials used are able to remove more plaque and buildup than your at-home process.  

7. Practice Professional Cleaning Aftercare 

After your professional dental cleanings, use a fluoride mouthwash to help prevent cavities and gum disease. Be sure to also practice any care you have been advised by your dentist to keep your teeth in good condition and prevent the development of any problems. 

8. Eat A Healthy Diet

This step will benefit more than just your teeth and gums. Eating a healthy diet is of course great for your general health, but it is also highly valuable for your oral health in particular. There are many foods that offer health benefits to your teeth and gums. Some of the best foods for your teeth include nuts and fatty fish. You will want to minimize the amount of sugary and starchy foods you eat in order to protect and maintain healthy teeth. 

9. Drink Plenty Of Water

Similarly to eating a healthy diet, an important step for oral health is drinking plenty of water throughout the day. Water helps to wash away food particles and harmful bacteria before they can settle on your teeth. Whenever possible, choose water over sugary beverage alternatives.  

Schedule An Appointment To Learn More About Deep Cleaning Teeth

Finally, one of the best things you can do to keep your teeth clean is schedule a checkup, particularly if it has been longer than a year since your last appointment. Your dentist will be able to provide you with further information and tips for continuing to maintain your oral health. Schedule an appointment with MidTown Dental Care today to learn more about deep cleaning teeth best practices.

  1. Floss, floss, floss! Here’s an analogy to think about…. would you wash just one of your hands after you use the restroom? No way! Not flossing is like only washing one of your hands. Brushing only gets at the exposed parts of your teeth – not the sides. Flossing finishes the job.

description: Why Do I Need X-Rays? Learn how digital dental x-rays at MidTown Dental Care help detect hidden issues safely and effectively.

html:
We hear this question from patients almost every day.  Why do I need x-rays?  Here are the top three most important reasons (and we’ve got good news about dental x-rays you may not know).

  1. The most important reason for having dental x-rays is to allow the dentist to provide a complete exam. A visual dental exam provides only some of the information a dentist needs to see.  Many cavities can only be seen on x-ray because they are in between teeth. Additionally, sometimes the only way to see abscesses, lesions or growths within the bony structures is via x-ray.
  2. We will only take the minimum number of xrays that any patient needs, as set out by the ADA guidelines and treatment requirements.
  3.  The radiographs we use in the dental office are DIGITAL radiographs. They use one tenth of the radiation other types of xrays use.  (You would get more radiation on a sunny day than you will receive from a full mouth set of dental xrays.)For all of these reasons, a dentist cannot conduct a complete exam unless x-rays are taken and evaluated.  We are always striving to perform the best treatment possible and one of the most important things we can do for our patients is to have up-to-date  xrays so we can properly evaluate their complete dental situation.

html:
When you need more than a cleaning…

A patient’s gum tissue (gingiva) is the foundation for a healthy mouth, and also provides the framework for healthy teeth.  Gum disease or (periodontal) disease is very common in adult patients, and is one of the first things we check during a new patient exam.

An important indicator of periodontal health is the depth of the space between each tooth and the gums. There is a space or “pocket” around each tooth, which is what a hygienist is measuring during an examination of the gum tissue.

A pocket depth of 1-3 millimeters is healthy, any space deeper than that (4-6 mm or more) may indicate gum disease is present. When a patient exhibits any signs of gum disease, a regular “cleaning” is not the answer.  Many times, a deeper cleaning (below the gum line) may be necessary.

Will it feel different?

A deep below the gum line cleaning usually feels the same as a regular dental cleaning, but it is most definitely different.  The hygienist is working below the gum line, cleaning areas that are not touched in a regular cleaning.

If it’s recommended you receive other procedures besides a regular cleaning, discuss it with your hygienist or dentist and I encourage you to invest the time and money to get your gums healthy again.

What goes around comes around

Gum disease is a cyclical disease. During one visit things may look healthy, and at another visit, early signs of gum disease might be present.  We always work with our patients to discuss options before any treatment is performed. The good news is there are many weapons to fight the early stages of gum disease—-ask us how we can help!

Mark Crego D.D.S.

What if I need a crown?

When a tooth has had a large filling for many years, or had a root canal for any reason, many times a dentist recommends your tooth be rebuilt with a crown or a “cap”.  In order to rebuild the tooth properly, a crown is often necessary to strengthen the tooth, and allow proper chewing function.

The process for getting a crown is not much different than any dental procedure.  A local anesthetic will be placed to numb the area being worked on, and then the tooth will be re-shaped, or “prepped” to accommodate the crown, which will completely cover the remaining tooth. A well done crown gives the appearance of a completely new, natural looking tooth.

The really great news is that today, MidTown Dental Care is able to complete the entire process in one visit.  Our patients walk out the door with a completed crown after one appointment, removing the need for a temporary crown and a second visit.

Crowns are made from an extremely strong ceramic material, and will last for many years. With proper home care by the patient (brushing and flossing) a crown will be an excellent investment in your oral health.  A crown functions just like a normal tooth, and prevents further damage to the tooth it is covering.  Crowns look natural, and can enhance a person’s smile as well as protect their tooth.

To find out more about the types of crowns available at our practice, please visit our website or call (414) 258-5351.

What is CEREC®?
Chairside Economical Restorations of Esthetic Ceramic or CEREC® for short is a new state-of-the-art method of reconstructing tooth restorations. CEREC® uses computer-assisted design (CAD) and computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) to offer single-day restorations for patients. This new technology has revolutionized ceramic restorations such as crowns and veneers for patients so that there is no longer a wait between preparing the restoration and finally receiving the finished product. With CEREC®, the technology is used while you are sitting in the dental chair, which is both economical for you and your dentist. The restorations created are metal-free and tooth colored to restore your tooth to its natural beauty, strength and function. With CEREC®’s CAD-CAM technology, these ceramic restorations can all be done in one single visit to the dentist.
The CEREC® Process
CEREC® uses CAD-CAM technology to design and mill custom restorations during one visit to the dentist. So how does this process work?

Exam and Preparation
Before you get started, your dentist will determine if CEREC® is right for you. Depending on how much healthy tooth structure you have remaining, it may be a simple filling or you may need a crown. After reviewing your options, the dentist will begin the process by administering anesthetic and preparing your tooth for restoration by removing decay and weakened tooth tissue.

Optical Impression
In order to make the desired restoration, a 3-dimensional image of the tooth that needs to be restored must be created from a digital camera scan of the tooth. This three-dimensional image will be used to create the restoration without the need to take a messy impression. This means no horrible tasting impression material for you to gag on. The computer and CEREC® 3D software then converts the digital image into a three-dimensional virtual model of the prepared tooth.

Milling Unit
This device is used to used to create the custom restoration needed for the tooth. Based on the original color of your tooth, the dentist is able to select the correct colored ceramic block and in a few minutes, the milling device is able to create the restoration needed.

Placing the Restoration
After the restoration is made, it is ready to be tried on to ensure that you get proper fit and bite. When it is ready, the restoration is polished and bonded into place by your dentist. Therefore, no temporary restoration is needed and no return trip is necessary, saving you time!

Advantages to Using CEREC®
CEREC® has revolutionized the restorative process. It was created with the patient in mind in order to make a visit to the dentist as pain-free as possible. Some of the benefits to using CEREC® are:

Most procedures can be done in one visit – less time-consuming
Less painful injections due to single-visit
No need to take messy impressions
No need to have a temporary restoration for in-between visits
Ability to save as much natural tooth structure as possible
Longer lasting restorations – may last over 10 years
Restores teeth to natural beauty, function and strength
Metal-free restorations
